andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh distributes land-title pattas to 26,401 families in Vijayawada
facts: Under the Pedalaku Pattabhishekam programme, pattas conveying full ownership rights were distributed to 26,401 families in Vijayawada.
The distribution covered about 707 acres in NTR and Krishna districts.
The land was valued at approximately ₹28,112 crore, according to reports of the event.
Earlier distributions cited by the Chief Minister included 28,000 families in Visakhapatnam and 5,800 in Mangalagiri.
andhraPradesh.summary: On 30 September, Andhra Pradesh distributed ownership pattas to 26,401 families at a programme in Vijayawada. The reported exercise covered land in NTR and Krishna districts and focused on formalising title for beneficiary households.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Land tenure, property rights, social justice and inclusive governance.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the programme name, beneficiary count and the districts covered: Pedalaku Pattabhishekam; 26,401 families; NTR and Krishna.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how secure land titles can strengthen household asset ownership and access to formal services, alongside the need for transparent beneficiary verification and clear land records.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Directly concerns land-title distribution to families in Vijayawada and the NTR and Krishna districts of Andhra Pradesh.

- **Status:** **COMPLETED**; distribution held in **Vijayawada** on **30 September 2026**
# 2. Scale and coverage
- **Beneficiaries:** **26,401 families**
- **Land covered:** About **707 acres** in **NTR** and **Krishna** districts
- **Reported land value:** Approximately **₹28,112 crore**

andhraPradesh.headline: Election Commission extends Andhra Pradesh electoral-roll revision schedule
facts: The Election Commission of India extended the schedule for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Andhra Pradesh.
The notice phase and disposal of claims and objections in Andhra Pradesh will continue until 10 October 2026.
Publication of the final electoral rolls in Andhra Pradesh is scheduled for 16 October 2026.
The extension was decided at an Election Commission meeting in New Delhi on 30 September 2026.
andhraPradesh.summary: The Election Commission extended key Andhra Pradesh milestones in its Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Claims and objections remain open through 10 October, with final rolls scheduled for publication on 16 October 2026.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Election Commission of India, electoral-roll preparation and the conduct of elections.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: For Andhra Pradesh’s SIR schedule, note 10 October 2026 for claims and objections and 16 October 2026 for final-roll publication.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine the importance of accurate electoral rolls and accessible claims-and-objections procedures for inclusive electoral participation and public confidence.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The revised dates apply directly to Andhra Pradesh’s electoral-roll revision.

andhraPradesh.headline: NIC Andhra Pradesh lists launch of Jeevandan cadaver-transplant monitoring web application

national.headline: Cabinet approves Green Energy Corridor Phase-III with 50 GWh of battery storage
facts: The Union Cabinet approved Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III) on 30 September 2026.
The scheme aims to strengthen intra-state transmission systems to evacuate up to 135 GW of renewable energy.
It includes deployment of 50 GWh of battery energy storage systems to support grid flexibility.
The total project outlay is ₹1,86,405 crore, including ₹54,082 crore in Central Financial Support.
The scheme is targeted for completion by FY 2032-33; State Transmission Utilities are the overall implementing agencies.
No direct AP-specific link established.
national.summary: The Union Cabinet approved GEC-III to expand intra-state transmission capacity and integrate renewable power, with 50 GWh of battery storage included. The stated target is to support evacuation of up to 135 GW of renewable energy by FY 2032-33; this is an approval, not a completed project.
national.staticLink: Renewable energy integration, electricity transmission and energy storage
national.prelimsTakeaway: Recall GEC-III’s 135 GW renewable-energy evacuation aim, 50 GWh BESS component, ₹1,86,405 crore outlay and FY 2032-33 target.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how transmission upgrades and storage can address renewable-energy intermittency while improving energy security and supporting a lower-carbon power system.

- **Scheme:** **Green Energy Corridor Phase-III (GEC-III)**
- **Objective:** Strengthen **intra-state transmission systems** to evacuate up to **135 GW** of renewable energy; support grid flexibility through battery energy storage systems
# 2. Key figures and implementation
| **Basis** | **Details** | **Details** |
|---|---|---|
| **Battery storage** | **50 GWh** | **Battery energy storage systems (BESS)** |
| **Project outlay** | **₹1,86,405 crore** | **Central Financial Support: ₹54,082 crore** |

national.headline: CCEA approves higher MSPs for six mandated Rabi crops for 2027-28
facts: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved higher MSPs for all six mandated Rabi crops for Marketing Season 2027-28.
MSP per quintal: wheat ₹2,610; barley ₹2,286; gram ₹5,958; lentil ₹7,390; rapeseed and mustard ₹6,613; safflower ₹7,215.
The largest absolute increase was for safflower, at ₹675 per quintal; rapeseed and mustard rose by ₹413 per quintal.
The announced margins over the stated cost of production ranged from 50% for safflower to 106% for wheat.
No direct AP-specific link established.
national.summary: On 30 September, the CCEA approved revised MSPs for the six mandated Rabi crops for the 2027-28 marketing season. Safflower received the largest absolute increase, while wheat had the highest stated margin over cost of production among the listed crops.
national.staticLink: Agricultural price policy, MSP and the cost of production
national.prelimsTakeaway: Know the six Rabi crops covered and the 2027-28 MSPs; safflower had the largest increase at ₹675 per quintal.
national.mainsAngle: Assess MSP as an instrument for price assurance and farm-income support, including the distinction between announcing a support price and actual procurement.

national.headline: Union Government releases monthly accounts through August 2026
facts: The Ministry of Finance published the Union Government’s consolidated accounts through August 2026 for FY 2026-27.
Total receipts were ₹13,67,709 crore, equal to 37.5% of the corresponding Budget Estimate.
Net tax revenue to the Centre was ₹8,37,921 crore; non-tax revenue was ₹4,54,549 crore; non-debt capital receipts were ₹75,239 crore.
Tax devolution to States was ₹5,90,391 crore, ₹60,243 crore below the corresponding previous-year amount.
Total expenditure was ₹20,77,958 crore, or 38.9% of the corresponding Budget Estimate; capital expenditure was ₹5,09,949 crore.
No direct AP-specific link established.
national.summary: The Ministry of Finance released the Union Government’s monthly accounts through August 2026 on 30 September. The release reported receipts, expenditure and tax devolution against the corresponding FY 2026-27 Budget Estimates; it is an interim fiscal update, not a full-year outturn.
national.staticLink: Union Budget, public finance and fiscal accounts
national.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish tax revenue, non-tax revenue, non-debt capital receipts, tax devolution and capital expenditure in the monthly accounts.
national.mainsAngle: Use the receipt and expenditure trends to discuss fiscal management, Centre-State transfers and the role of capital expenditure in public investment.

national.headline: ₹5,547.99 crore of PSS procurement approved for Kharif pulses and oilseeds in three states

national.headline: Cabinet approves Intelligent Traffic Management System for 42 Delhi corridors
facts: The Cabinet approved Delhi Police’s Intelligent Traffic Management System project at an estimated cost of ₹1,789.52 crore, inclusive of taxes.
The project covers 42 identified traffic corridors and is to be implemented in three phases over 24 months.
The plan includes AI-enabled adaptive traffic signals, technology-based enforcement and real-time traffic information.
The system is intended to facilitate ambulance priority and quicker responses to congestion and road incidents.
The approval included five years of operation and maintenance after implementation.
No direct AP-specific link established.
national.summary: The Cabinet approved an ITMS project for 42 Delhi traffic corridors, with implementation planned in three phases over 24 months. Its announced functions include adaptive signals, real-time traffic information and ambulance prioritisation; the project was approved, not yet completed.
national.staticLink: Urban governance, intelligent transport systems and smart mobility
national.prelimsTakeaway: The approved project is for Delhi: 42 corridors, ₹1,789.52 crore and a planned 24-month, three-phase implementation.
national.mainsAngle: Evaluate how urban data systems can improve mobility and emergency response, while considering interoperability, privacy and maintenance requirements.

international.headline: WHO issues guidance to prevent heat-related illness at mass gatherings
facts: WHO published its guidance suite, Prevention and management of heat-related illness at mass gatherings, on 30 September 2026.
The evidence review covered studies from 1980 to 2025, documenting nearly 500,000 medical encounters and over 22,000 heat-related illnesses.
The review found that well-organised on-site medical systems can treat more than 90% of patients at event venues.
Recommended measures include safe drinking water, cooling facilities, schedule adjustments, crowd-flow management, real-time surveillance and prepared on-site medical services.
international.summary: WHO’s new guidance treats extreme heat at mass gatherings as a public-health, preparedness and operational risk. It calls for whole-of-event planning across water and sanitation, venue design, transport, communications and health services.
international.staticLink: Heat-health action plans; climate-change adaptation; disaster preparedness and public-health emergency management.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the WHO guidance title and its integrated measures: water, cooling, scheduling, crowd management, surveillance and on-site care.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how heat risks at large events require coordinated planning by health authorities, event organisers and local services, rather than reliance on individual precautions alone.

- **Risk framing:** Extreme heat at mass gatherings as a **public-health, preparedness and operational risk**
> Exam angle: Test the WHO guidance title, evidence figures and integrated heat-risk measures at mass gatherings.

international.headline: WIPO Global Innovation Index 2026 ranks India 38th
facts: WIPO released the 19th edition of the Global Innovation Index on 29 September 2026, ranking 139 economies using 79 indicators.
India ranked 38th; Switzerland, Sweden, the United States, the Republic of Korea and Singapore occupied the top five positions.
The index assesses innovation inputs and outputs, including research and development, infrastructure, skills, high-technology trade and intellectual-property-related indicators.
WIPO reported that India and Viet Nam had remained innovation overperformers for 16 consecutive years.
international.summary: The 2026 WIPO index placed India 38th among 139 economies, with Switzerland at the top. It provides a comparative measure of innovation ecosystems and highlights the policy challenge of turning research, skills and investment into broad-based innovation outputs.

international.prelimsTakeaway: WIPO publishes the annual Global Innovation Index; in its 2026 edition India ranked 38th and Switzerland ranked first.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how India can strengthen research foundations, technology adoption and firm-level innovation while sustaining its relative strength in innovation outputs.

international.headline: FIS recognises climate action by ski organisers, athletes and national associations
facts: The International Ski and Snowboard Federation’s second Climate Awards recognised climate action across local organising committees, athletes and national ski associations.
Val Gardena, Italy, received the Best Local Organising Committee award after reporting a 21.6% reduction in total emissions year-on-year.
Canada’s Marion Thénault won the Best Athlete award; France received the Best National Ski Association award.
At the accompanying Viessmann Combined For Change awards, Otepää, Estonia, and Trondheim, Norway, received awards for CO₂ calculation and greenhouse-gas reduction, respectively.
international.summary: FIS recognised sustainability work in snow sports at its Geneva autumn meetings. The awards highlighted emissions measurement and reduction efforts by event organisers, athletes and national associations.
international.staticLink: Climate action; sustainable sports-event management; measurement and reduction of greenhouse-gas emissions.
international.prelimsTakeaway: FIS’s second Climate Awards recognised Val Gardena, Marion Thénault and France in the Best LOC, Best Athlete and Best NSA categories.
international.mainsAngle: Use sports-event emissions management to illustrate how climate action can be incorporated into transport, procurement, venue operations and organisational planning.

mcqs.question: According to the WIPO Global Innovation Index 2026, which statement is correct?
options: India ranked 38th, and the index assessed 139 economies using 79 indicators.
India ranked 28th, and the index assessed 139 economies using 79 indicators.
India ranked 38th, and the index assessed 129 economies using 79 indicators.
India ranked 48th, and the index assessed 139 economies using 89 indicators.
mcqs.explanation: WIPO released the 19th edition on 29 September 2026; India ranked 38th among 139 economies assessed using 79 indicators.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes Green Energy Corridor Phase-III as approved by the Union Cabinet?
options: It aims to evacuate up to 135 GW of renewable energy and includes 50 GWh of battery storage.
It aims to evacuate up to 50 GW of renewable energy and includes 135 GWh of battery storage.
It aims to evacuate up to 135 GW of renewable energy and includes 5 GWh of battery storage.
It aims to evacuate up to 135 GW of renewable energy and includes no battery storage.
mcqs.explanation: GEC-III is designed to strengthen intra-state transmission, with up to 135 GW of renewable-energy evacuation and 50 GWh of battery storage.

mcqs.question: For Marketing Season 2027-28, which Rabi crop had an announced MSP of ₹7,390 per quintal?
options: Wheat
Gram
Lentil
Safflower
mcqs.explanation: The approved MSP for lentil was ₹7,390 per quintal. Safflower's MSP was ₹7,215 per quintal.

mcqs.question: In the Union Government accounts through August 2026, what was the reported capital expenditure?
mcqs.explanation: Capital expenditure was ₹5,09,949 crore. The other figures correspond respectively to net tax revenue, total receipts and total expenditure.

mcqs.question: Which statement about the draft Petroleum (Amendment) Bill, 2026, is correct?
options: It was enacted on 30 September 2026, with comments invited until 30 October.
It was released for consultation, with comments invited until 30 October 2026.
It was approved by Parliament, with comments invited until 30 September 2027.
It was released for consultation, with comments invited until 10 October 2026.
mcqs.explanation: The Ministry released the draft for stakeholder and public consultation on 30 September 2026; it remained a draft, with comments invited until 30 October.

mcqs.question: Under the Pedalaku Pattabhishekam programme in Vijayawada, pattas were distributed to how many families?
mcqs.explanation: Pattas conveying full ownership rights were distributed to 26,401 families, covering about 707 acres in NTR and Krishna districts.

mcqs.question: What was the revised schedule for Andhra Pradesh's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls?
options: Claims and objections until 10 October 2026; final rolls on 16 October 2026.
Claims and objections until 16 October 2026; final rolls on 30 October 2026.
Claims and objections until 30 September 2026; final rolls on 10 October 2026.
Claims and objections until 10 November 2026; final rolls on 16 November 2026.
mcqs.explanation: The Election Commission extended the notice phase and disposal of claims and objections until 10 October, with final rolls scheduled for 16 October 2026.

mcqs.question: The Jeevandan-Andhra Pradesh web application listed by NIC Andhra Pradesh is intended for monitoring which activity?
